acceptedFindings.title: Primary result omitted from manuscript
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript fails to state the correlation coefficient (r=0.658) and p-value, making it impossible to assess the study's main finding. This omission prevents any meaningful review or interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add the Pearson correlation coefficient, its 95% confidence interval, p-value, and sample size to the Results section and Abstract.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the manuscript now contains numeric output from stats-run.json (correlation=0.6579, p=3.87e-31, n=240).

acceptedFindings.title: No diagnostic checks for Pearson correlation assumptions
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Pearson requires linearity, bivariate normality, and homoscedasticity. Violations can invalidate the correlation coefficient and p-value.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Run and document diagnostic plots (residuals vs. fitted, Q-Q), normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk), and consider robust alternatives (e.g., Spearman) if violations are present.

acceptedFindings.title: No verification of Pearson correlation assumptions
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Pearson correlation assumes linearity, bivariate normality, and absence of influential outliers. Without checks, the estimated r=0.658 may be misleading.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a scatterplot with LOESS smoother, test for normality (Shapiro-Wilk), and report outlier diagnostics. If assumptions fail, consider Spearman correlation or transformation.

acceptedFindings.title: Variable definitions and measurement missing
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without knowing what 'severity' and 'outcome_cont' represent (e.g., clinical scale, units, range), the clinical relevance and potential floor/ceiling effects cannot be judged.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Describe each variable: what it measures, how it was collected, its possible range, and any known validation. Provide summary statistics (mean, SD, min, max).

acceptedFindings.title: No adjustment for potential confounders
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Observational association can be confounded. Even if no causal claim is made, the raw correlation may over- or underestimate the true relationship and limits the interpretation of the strength of linear association.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either adjust for known confounders (if available) or explicitly state that no confounders were measured and discuss this as a key limitation in the Discussion.

acceptedFindings.title: Diagnostics artifact contains only test name and sample size
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: No evidence that assumption checks were performed or inspected, making the analysis irreproducible and the result suspect.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Extend the diagnostics.json to include numeric and visual results for normality, linearity, and outlier detection.

acceptedFindings.title: Confidence interval for correlation not reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A point estimate (0.658) alone is insufficient; a 95% CI communicates the precision of the estimate and is essential for interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report a 95% confidence interval for the Pearson correlation coefficient.

acceptedFindings.title: No description of missing data handling or complete-case exclusions
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can introduce selection bias if missingness is related to exposure or outcome; readers cannot assess the impact without details.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report number of records excluded, reasons, compare included/excluded groups on available variables, and discuss potential bias.

acceptedFindings.title: No evidence of data range, distribution, or outlier inspection
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Non-normal distributions or extreme outliers can distort Pearson correlation, yet the data are unchecked.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide summary statistics (min, max, mean, SD, skewness) and visualizations (histograms, boxplots) before correlation.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing data handling not described
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The analysis uses 240 complete cases, but the original sample size and proportion of missingness are unknown. Non-random missingness could bias the correlation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the initial sample size, number excluded for missing data, and compare demographics of excluded vs. included subjects if possible. If not, acknowledge as limitation.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript states advisory issues found, but QA records show none
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Creates confusion: either the manuscript is outdated, or the QA process missed real issues. Inconsistent reporting undermines trust.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: If real issues exist, list them; otherwise, remove the generic advisory warning from the manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Extremely small p-value reported without effect size interpretation
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A p-value of 3.87e-31 does not convey practical significance; the manuscript fails to contextualize the correlation magnitude (e.g., R² = 0.43).
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add interpretation of the correlation strength (e.g., 'large effect') and its practical meaning, along with the CI.

acceptedFindings.title: Ethical approval and data provenance not stated
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Medical/public-health studies must disclose ethical review and data source per reporting guidelines (e.g., STROBE).
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a statement on institutional review board (IRB) approval or exemption, and source of the dataset.

acceptedFindings.title: Figure caption lacks descriptive detail
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The caption 'Scatterplot for the two variables used in the correlation run' does not guide interpretation or mention observed trend.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Revise caption to note the linear association, strength, and any notable patterns (e.g., 'strong positive linear relationship, r = 0.66').
